dedupe_keys.name: wmost watershed management optimization support tool us epa

description: WMOST is a decision support tool for integrated water management at the local or small watershed scale. It models flows and water quality in a spatially lumped watershed at daily or monthly steps and uses nonlinear programming to find the least-cost mix of management options, including stormwater practices and green infrastructure, combined sewer overflow controls, stream restoration, water demand and infrastructure measures and agricultural practices, to meet water quality criteria, load targets or CSO limits. The US Environmental Protection Agency develops, distributes and supports it as public-domain software, with releases from version 1 (2013) to 3.1 (2022), a benefits module, and the WMOST Climate Automation Programs (August 2024) that automate climate scenario runs with SWAT and HAWQS; it is free to download from the EPA page, with a user guide, theoretical documentation and training videos. Coverage is national for US watersheds of HUC10 to HUC12 size. Caveats: it is a screening tool with lumped spatial detail, and it runs in Excel. Simulation uses: optimising stormwater, CSO and water supply investments for capacity planning and climate adaptation. Related records: HAWQS (platform-hawqs-hydrologic-water-quality-system) and EPA SWMM (model-epa-swmm).
inputs: Watershed hydrology and water quality time series (for example from SWAT or HSPF via the Hydroprocessor or HCAM)
Costs and performance of management options (stormwater BMPs and green infrastructure, CSO controls, water demand, infrastructure, riparian buffers, agricultural BMPs)
Targets such as water quality criteria, pollutant load limits or CSO reduction
licence: Public domain (EPA software, as the EPA page describes it)
